channel.title: Cato on The Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Cato on The Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Cato I
item.description: Urges citizens to critically examine the proposed Constitution themselves, emphasizing the importance of informed public judgment.

item.title: Cato II
item.description: Criticizes the tone and approach of Federalist writings, particularly those by “Caesar” (Alexander Hamilton), for being arrogant and dismissive.

item.title: Cato III
item.description: Argues that the vast size and diversity of the United States make a consolidated republic impractical and prone to aristocratic dominance.

item.title: Cato IV
item.description: Warns that the proposed presidency, with its extensive powers and lack of term limits, could evolve into a monarchy-like authority.

item.title: Cato V
item.description: Expresses concern over the potential for the federal government to become a corrupt aristocracy, undermining republican principles.

item.title: Cato VI
item.description: Highlights the dangers of centralized power and the potential erosion of state sovereignty under the new Constitution.

item.title: Cato VII
item.description: Continues the critique of the executive branch, emphasizing the risks of unchecked presidential power and the absence of sufficient checks and balances.
